persona.bio: Nina, 36, ecommerce manager at a home goods brand. She runs the Shopify store: product pages, launches, discount codes, the email flows in Klaviyo, customer service escalations in Gorgias, and weekly sales numbers in Google Sheets. She writes product descriptions for every new item, plans promotions with the team over Gmail and Slack, and chases suppliers for images and specs. She uses ChatGPT and Claude every day. Her company encourages AI, and she can connect her work Gmail.

path.role: You’re the ecommerce manager at a home goods brand, running the Shopify store day to day.

steps.note: I’m the ecommerce manager at a home goods brand, and I run our online store day to day. I write product descriptions, promo emails and replies to customers. I write to shoppers who want clear, honest details about what they are buying. My tone is warm, plain and confident, never pushy. I like short sentences and tight copy that fits a product page. Keep the fabric, size and care details I give you, and never add details I did not give you, like materials, measurements, prices or claims. If something is missing, ask me or leave a square bracket. Give me a draft I can read and change before it goes live.

steps.title: Your product descriptions, with a saved assistant
steps.read: Your product descriptions now live in a saved ChatGPT project that already knows your voice and your store. You hand it the product details, and it gives back copy that fits the page and keeps the fabric facts. That is better in your job because every listing sounds like your brand, and you stop re explaining it each time.

material.label: Instructions for your assistant
items: You are my writing assistant for product descriptions at a home goods brand. I’m the ecommerce manager and I run our Shopify store. I paste in product details from Shopify or a Sheet, and sometimes an existing description that runs too long. Write for shoppers who want clear, honest details. Keep the tone warm, plain and confident, with short sentences. Keep every fabric, size, care and material detail I give you. Never add details I did not give you, and never invent claims, prices or measurements. If something is missing, put it in square brackets and tell me. Keep copy short enough to fit a product page, and avoid filler like ’perfect for any home’. Give me back one tightened description first, then a one line version for a product card. Flag anything you cut so I can check it.

material.label: Examples to start with
items: Before: The new [product name] is made from [fabric] and is a wonderful addition to any room, bringing comfort and style that you will love for years to come. It measures [size] and is machine washable. After: [Product name] is made from [fabric]. It measures [size] and is machine washable. Soft, easy to style and ready for everyday use.

Before: Can you tighten the copy on the new [product name]? It’s too long for the product page and I need it live before [launch day]. Keep the fabric details. After: [Product name] in [fabric], [size]. [One line on how it feels or looks.] Care: [care instructions].

Before: Our [product name] is handcrafted with care using [material], and every piece is a little different, which makes it special in your home. After: [Product name] is made with [material]. Each piece varies slightly. [Size and care details].

steps.title: Your customer message replies, drafted in your inbox
steps.read: Your customer replies get drafted right inside Gmail, and you check each one before you send. You type a short line about what you want to say, and the draft fills in the rest. That is better in your job because each reply still sounds like you, without starting from a blank box.

material.label: Your starting lines
items: Reply to a customer asking where their order is. Say I’m checking on it and will update them by [day]. Warm and short.
Reply to a customer who got a damaged item. Say I’m sorry, and ask for a photo of the damage and their order number.
Reply to a customer asking about a return. Say I can help, and explain the steps from [our return policy]. Keep it friendly.
Reply to a customer asking about the size or fabric of [product name]. Share these details: [details]. Don’t add anything else.
Reply to a customer asking when [product name] is back in stock. Say I don’t have a date yet and offer [what we can do].
Reply to a customer who wants to change their order address. Say what I can do before it ships: [details].
Reply to an unhappy customer. Thank them for telling me, say what I’ll do next: [next step], and keep it calm and plain.

material.label: Notes on your tone
items: Press Friendly when a draft sounds stiff or like a form letter, especially for shoppers asking simple questions.
Press Shorten when a draft runs long, like order status updates, where a customer wants the answer fast.
Press Formalize only for serious issues, like a complaint or a damaged item, and reread it to make sure it still sounds warm.
If a draft makes a promise I did not type, such as a date, refund or policy, I fix it or delete it before I send.

safeUse: Never type customer names, home addresses, phone numbers, emails or order numbers into a chat tool. Use square brackets instead.
Never paste payment details or anything from a customer’s account.
Keep unreleased products, launch dates and pricing out of chats unless my company says it is OK.
Check every product detail, like fabric, size and care, against my own product data before it goes live.
Read every description and every customer reply before it goes out, and send it myself.
steps.askMessage: Hi [manager’s name], I’d like to confirm which AI tools the company has approved and what I may use them for. I have two tasks in mind: drafting product descriptions in ChatGPT, and drafting customer replies inside Gmail with Help me write. I would only use product details, never customer names, addresses or order numbers, and I would read everything before it goes out. Can you tell me what is approved, or point me to who can?

design.today: You rewrite product descriptions about once a day, often from copy that runs too long. You copy the product details from Shopify or paste them from a Sheet into ChatGPT or Claude.
design.newWay: You set up a saved assistant that already knows your brand voice, your length limit for the product page and the rule to keep fabric details. Each day you paste in the product details and the long copy, and it gives back a tightened version in your format. You read it and paste it into Shopify yourself, so the copy stays consistent across launches like Friday's without you re-explaining it each time.

steps.goal: Pick two or three of your best live product descriptions and note your length limit and which details must always stay, like fabric and care.
Make a project for product descriptions so your voice and rules are kept in one place.
Save the assistant instructions and your example descriptions so each new description follows the same shape.
Save short notes about you and your brand tone so every chat starts with them.
Test it on the linen throw copy and adjust the instructions until the length and fabric details are right.
